title: Emergent Dimensionality in Diluted Power-Law Quantum Walks
abstract: We investigate single-excitation quantum walks across the one-to-two-dimensional crossover in diluted power-law hopping models. Using arrays of $\ell$ coupled chains of length $L$, we identify the finite-size localization crossover from the longitudinal spreading of an initially localized excitation. The crossover filling is well described by an exponential approach to its two-dimensional value with increasing $\ell$, defining a characteristic transverse scale $\ell_e$, and effectively two-dimensional behavior emerges already for $\ell\ll L$. An independent spectral analysis shows that $\ell_e$ is set by the transverse extent of the eigenstates participating in the dynamics, providing a microscopic interpretation of the dimensional crossover. Our results reveal an intrinsic eigenstate scale governing emergent dimensionality in diluted systems with power-law hopping, a regime directly relevant to recently developed arrays of polar molecules, Rydberg atoms, and other quantum simulators with long-range interactions.
summary: This work analyzes quantum walks on disordered lattices with long-range hopping to understand the dimensional crossover from 1D to 2D. The key finding is that this crossover is not arbitrary but is dictated by an intrinsic transverse eigenstate scale ($\ell_e$). This establishes a fundamental link between the transport dynamics and the underlying quantum structure of the disordered system.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the dimensionality of quantum transport emerges in systems with long-range, power-law hopping interactions when disorder is present.
main_result: The crossover from 1D to effective 2D behavior is governed by a characteristic transverse scale ($\ell_e$), which is microscopically determined by the transverse extent of the system's eigenstates.
method: The study uses numerical analysis of the finite-size localization crossover filling ($ho_c$) via exponential fitting, complemented by independent spectral analysis of eigenstate spatial extents.
model_or_system: The model consists of single-excitation quantum walks on arrays of $\ell$ coupled chains of length $L$, featuring hopping governed by a power-law decay $J_{ij} \propto |r-r'|^{-\alpha}$ and incorporating dilution-induced disorder.
key_observables: Longitudinal spreading width ($\eta(t)$), finite-size localization crossover filling ($ho_c$), and the characteristic transverse scale ($\ell_e$).
important_parameters: Hopping exponent ($\alpha$), transverse width ($\ell$), system length ($L$), and disorder filling ($ho$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes open boundary conditions and averages over many disorder realizations; approximations are used to relate the crossover filling to the eigenstate structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of spreading ($\eta(t)$) across different $\ell$ and $\alpha$, and compare the derived crossover scale ($\ell_e$) against the calculated transverse eigenstate extent ($ ar{\xi}$).
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the longitudinal spreading and identifies the crossover filling ($ho_c$) using finite-size scaling. It then derives the characteristic scale $\ell_e$ from this fit and independently verifies this scale by comparing it to the transverse extent of the relevant eigenstates, establishing the microscopic link.
why_interesting: The direct connection found between the transport-derived scale ($\ell_e$) and the intrinsic eigenstate structure ($ ar{\xi}$) provides a powerful, non-perturbative understanding of how dimensionality emerges in complex, disordered quantum systems, which is highly relevant to quantum simulators.

Figure 2(c) shows ηmax versus filling ρ for α = 3. In one dimension, ηmax decreases rapidly upon dilution, whereas in the two-dimensional limit it remains close to L over a broad high-filling regime. Upon decreasing ρ, ηmax de- velops an inflection point at ρ2D c ≃0.58, followed by a rapid suppression of transport. We identify this inflection point with the finite-size localization crossover filling ρc, following Refs. [7, 14]. For intermediate ℓ, ρc lies between the one- and two-dimensional limits, providing the dy- namical signature of the dimensional crossover analyzed below.
